items.text: REFERRED TO VETERANS, HOMELAND SECURITY AND MILITARY AFFAIRS
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO VETERANS, HOMELAND SECURITY AND MILITARY AFFAIRS
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the activation of 2-1-1 New
York state upon declaration of a state disaster emergency
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8553

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the activation of
2-1-1 New York state upon declaration of a state disaster emergency

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this legislation is to include 2-1-1 services as a part
of the State's emergency disaster plan and provide for its continued
activation during an emergency.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Subdivision 1 of Section 21 of the Executive Law is amended
to add the chief professional officer of 2-1-1 New York to the State
preparedness commission.

Section 2: The executive law is amended by adding a new section 28-b
which would activate the 2-1-1 system when a state disaster emergency is
declared.

Section 3: Establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to the United Way, there are approximately 1.5 million nonpro-
fit organizations in the United States, plus thousands of government
agencies. Finding health and human services help can be confusing and
intimidating, leaving many people not knowing where to start. That is
why 2-1-1 was developed--as an easy-to-remember phone number for people
in need of help.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) set aside 2-1-1 as the
number to use nationally for health and human services information and
referral in 1999, they directed telephone providers to work with organ-
izations like United Way to implement the service. Subsequently New
York's Public Service Commission assigned the number to 2-1-1 New York
to develop the service on a statewide basis.

2-1-1 contact centers are staffed by trained specialists who quickly
assess the callers' needs and refer them to the help they need. 2-1-1
services are free, confidential, and accessible to everyone through
multilingual capabilities. Information is also available online through
comprehensive regional databases of government and nonprofit services.

While initially developed with access to day-to-day human services in
mind, 2-1-1 in NYS has proven to be an asset in disaster response and
long-term recovery. 2-1-1 relieves 911 and other government agencies of
calls for non-emergency assistance during and after a disaster.  Past
examples in New York State include snow and ice storms, flooding, as
well as Hurricane Irene and Superstorm Sandy.

2-1-1 has grown to be a critical resource for our communities in times
of natural disaster and during the Covid pandemic response by providing
reliable, up-to-date, relevant information for those impacted, first
responders, and long-term groups. This legislation recognizes the impor-
tance of the 2-1-1 system and includes the program in the State's disas-
ter plan and calls for its continued activation during disaster and will
serve as a public information in coordination with emergency management
professionals.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is new legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

This legislation will have no fiscal implications for State or local
governments.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
